analysis.title: The Day Ahead - North America, Friday, November 6, 2026
key_insights: The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to 24,315, its deepest one-day drop in 19 months, confirming a correction. The S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73 and the Dow fell 3.44% to 51,523.06.

Chipmakers led the drop on fears of tougher AI regulation after Democrats won control of Congress in Tuesday's midterms, including in states where data center growth is contentious. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index fell 12.25% to 9,011.14 and Nvidia fell 9.26%.

Big tech stocks lost about $2 trillion, the biggest decline since the 'Liberation Day' rout last year. Neocloud firms such as Nebius and CoreWeave have faced financing concerns since US interest rates rose late in the summer.

Treasuries rallied as equities fell. The 10-year yield fell to 4.8347% (+14/32 in price), the 30-year to 5.2571% and the 2-year to 4.4623%. FHN Financial's Will Compernolle tied the bid for Treasuries to the shift away from chipmaker stocks.

Brent rose 4.20% to $98.59 and WTI rose 3.01% to $90.77 on new tanker attacks and caution about a quick normalization of oil flows in the US-Israeli war with Iran. Investors also noted Iran's unchanged position on negotiations with the US.
Spot gold rose 0.64% to $4,085.59. Metals trader Tai Wong said a stronger-than-expected payrolls print would likely confirm an already highly expected December rate hike.
Convera's Kevin Ford cited market pricing for back-to-back Fed hikes at the end of this year and the start of next. The dollar index was roughly unchanged at 101.58.

Today's October jobs report (0930 ET) is forecast at +65,000 nonfarm payrolls versus +29,000 prior, with unemployment steady at 4.2%. Average hourly earnings are forecast at +0.3% m/m and +2.9% y/y. Preliminary November U Mich sentiment is forecast at 48.

Initial jobless claims fell 6,000 to 189,000 for the week ended October 31, a 57-year low tied with mid-July, against a Reuters poll forecast of 196,000. Challenger job cuts were 43,994 in October, up 2% from September and the lowest for any October since 2023.
Fed's Hammack and Barkin favored a gradual rate-hike path to lower above-target inflation, in the first Fed comments after the midterms.

OpenAI said it will stop using non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating data center sites. The change is part of an effort to win over local communities after the Democratic wins.

SpaceX fell 9.05% to $123.62 and Tesla fell 10.77% to $343.69. More than half of SpaceX's Q3 sales came from renting out computing capacity. Texas Democrats won the Senate, governor and attorney general races.

About 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips are stored in Hong Kong awaiting shipment to mainland China because Beijing is withholding large-scale import approval. Several major Chinese internet companies have each obtained about 10,000 H200 chips in recent months.
Tapestry raised its annual revenue and profit outlook and beat Q1 revenue estimates, with China revenue up 43%. The shares rose 7% to $134.09.
Tripadvisor fell 27.65% to $7.38 after its CEO and CFO announced departures and it said it will cut about 425 roles.

ConocoPhillips beat Q3 adjusted profit estimates and raised its quarterly dividend by nearly 11% to 93 cents from 84 cents. Q3 production was 2.3 million boepd, with Q4 guidance of 2.32 to 2.36 million boepd.
Cigna raised its annual profit forecast after beating Q3 estimates and expects adjusted profit growth of at least 10% in 2027. Evernorth adjusted revenue was $63.77B, up about 6%.
Banks expect tougher congressional oversight, including cost-of-living and consumer finance probes and efforts against AI-driven fraud.
Investors are watching for a debt-ceiling standoff after the Democratic sweep.

Canada's TSX fell 2.03% to 35,605.27 and Canadian tech fell 3.77% as the chip and AI selloff spread. Canadian Natural, TC Energy and Bombardier posted beats or raised guidance, and Nutrien missed on earnings.

Lumentum fell 17.30% to $518.30 in the chip and AI selloff.
Western Digital fell 16.86% to $269.24 in the chip and AI selloff.

Tapestry raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts and beat Q1 revenue estimates, with Coach strength in North America and China revenue up 43%.
Tripadvisor fell 27.65% after its CEO and CFO announced departures and it said AI tools are pressuring its hotel-search business.
ConocoPhillips beat Q3 adjusted profit estimates on higher oil prices and raised its dividend by nearly 11%.
Cigna beat Q3 estimates and raised its annual profit forecast, with Evernorth and healthcare unit revenue up.
Ralph Lauren raised its annual outlook but guided Q3 revenue growth below Wall Street expectations.
Wendy's rejected a $1.4B take-private offer from Trian and adopted a poison pill.

sector_views.rationale: Chipmakers and neoclouds led the selloff on fears that tighter AI regulation and data center delays will slow the buildout.
Brent and WTI rose and ConocoPhillips and Canadian Natural beat estimates on higher oil prices.
Banks expect tougher congressional oversight on consumer finance and AI-driven fraud.
HCA, Tenet and UHS cite rising uninsured patients squeezing margins and expected Medicaid and ACA coverage losses ahead of 2027.

earnings_insights: Tapestry (reported 11/5): beat fiscal Q1 revenue estimates and raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts. China revenue rose 43%. Shares closed up 7% at $134.09.

ConocoPhillips (reported 11/5): beat Q3 adjusted profit estimates. Realized price was $61.40 per boe, up 32% y/y. Production was 2.3M boepd vs 2.4M a year earlier. Q4 production guidance is 2.32-2.36M boepd.
Cigna (reported 11/5): beat Q3 estimates and raised its annual adjusted profit forecast. Evernorth adjusted revenue was $63.77B, up about 6%. Pharmacy benefit services profit fell 22% to $765M.

TC Energy (reported 11/5): Q3 adjusted EPS of C$0.94 vs LSEG consensus of C$0.86. 2026 adjusted core profit guidance raised to C$11.8-12.0B from C$11.6-11.8B. 2027 guidance of C$12.3-12.5B has a midpoint slightly above the C$12.35B consensus.
Canadian Natural (reported 11/5): Q3 adjusted EPS of C$1.65 vs LSEG consensus of C$1.45. Output was 1.65M boepd vs 1.62M a year earlier.
Nutrien (reported 11/5): Q3 EPS of $0.61 vs consensus of $0.80. Management expects strong potash demand and weak nitrogen fertilizer sales.
Bombardier (reported 11/5): Q3 revenue of $2.37B vs $2.38B estimate. Free cash flow of $183M vs $159.5M estimate. 2026 free cash flow guidance raised to more than $1.3B from more than $1B.
Ralph Lauren (reported 11/5): raised its annual outlook but guided Q3 revenue growth below Wall Street expectations.
Carlyle (reported 11/5): Q3 profit beat estimates on higher asset sales.

Upcoming 11/6 (LSEG consensus, not yet reported): Charter Q3 EPS est $6.68 (Smart Estimate) / $8.03 (mean), revenue est $15,105.39M. Humana Q3 EPS est -$1.01, revenue est $40,889.96M. Moderna Q3 EPS est -$1.32, revenue est $885.05M. Vistra Q3 EPS est $2.88, revenue est $6,024.05M. PPL Q3 EPS est $0.54. Franklin Templeton FQ4 EPS est $0.77.
Enbridge is expected to report Q3 adjusted EPS of C$0.51 per LSEG estimates (forecast, not yet reported).

vol_and_positioning: No VIX or options data in the text. Equities fell sharply, with the Nasdaq in a correction and the semiconductor index down 12.25% in one session.
geopolitical: The US-Israeli war on Iran has disrupted oil supplies. Tanker strikes on mines and drone attacks continue, and Iran's position on negotiations with the US is unchanged.
Beijing is withholding approval for large-scale imports of Nvidia H200 chips, with about 600,000 stored in Hong Kong.
Democrats won control of the US Congress in Tuesday's midterms, raising expectations of investigations, AI and data center regulation, and a possible debt-ceiling standoff.
US tariffs on Canadian kitchen cabinets are set to double to 50% on January 1.

tension_points.bull_case: Strategists see it as unlikely that new lawmakers can stop the buildout altogether. OpenAI is changing its community policies to win support for data centers.
tension_points.bear_case: Any slowdown in data center development would hurt the AI growth story, which has largely depended on rapid infrastructure buildout (SimCorp's Melissa Brown). Neocloud financing concerns add to the pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence that newly elected members and governors succeed in slowing data center approvals would confirm the bear case.

tension_points.theme: Fed rate hike path and payrolls
tension_points.bull_case: Weekly jobless claims at a 57-year low show labor market resilience.
tension_points.bear_case: A stronger-than-expected payrolls print would likely confirm an already highly expected December rate hike (Tai Wong), which raises the opportunity cost of holding gold.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weaker-than-expected October payrolls print versus the 65,000 forecast would challenge the December hike expectation.
